questions.question: The plasma membrane is composed of _____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**lipids and proteins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **plasma membrane**, also referred to as the **cell membrane**, is a biological membrane that separates the interior of all cells from the outside environment. It is primarily composed of **lipids** and **proteins**.
 
• The **lipids** are arranged in a **bilayer** (two layers), providing a basic structural framework for the membrane. These lipids are mostly **phospholipids**, which have a **hydrophilic** (water-loving) head and **hydrophobic** (water-fearing) tails.
 
• **Proteins** are another major component, accounting for about **50 percent** of the membrane's mass in many cell types. They are responsible for most of the membrane's specific functions, such as **transport**, **enzymatic activity**, and **signal transduction**.
 
• The specific ratio of **lipids to proteins** varies depending on the type of cell; for instance, a **human erythrocyte** (red blood cell) membrane contains approximately **52 percent protein** and **40 percent lipids**.
 
• The option **lipids and proteins** is correct because they form the fundamental structure of the **Fluid Mosaic Model**. **DNA** is found in the **nucleus** or **mitochondria**, and **sugars** (carbohydrates) are only minor components attached to the outer surface. ***Hence, the statement B is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fluid Mosaic Model**: This widely accepted model was proposed by **S.J. Singer** and **Garth L. Nicolson** in the year **1972**. It describes the plasma membrane as a **fluid combination** of phospholipids, cholesterol, and proteins.
 
• **Membrane Lipids**: The most abundant lipids in the membrane are **phosphoglycerides**. Additionally, **cholesterol** molecules are interspersed among the phospholipids in **animal cells** to maintain membrane **fluidity** and **stability** at various temperatures.
 
• **Membrane Proteins**: These are categorized based on their ease of extraction. **Integral proteins** (intrinsic) are buried partially or totally in the lipid bilayer, while **peripheral proteins** (extrinsic) lie on the surface of the membrane.
 
• **Carbohydrates**: Found on the exterior surface of cells, they are linked to proteins (forming **glycoproteins**) or to lipids (forming **glycolipids**). These **carbohydrate chains** play a key role in **cell-to-cell recognition** and **immune response**.
 
• **Selectively Permeable**: One of the most important **functions** of the plasma membrane is that it is **selectively permeable**. This means it allows the passage of certain molecules (like **oxygen** and **carbon dioxide**) through **simple diffusion** while blocking others, requiring **carrier proteins** or **ion channels** for transport.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Active and Passive Transport**: The plasma membrane facilitates **passive transport** (movement along the **concentration gradient** without energy) and **active transport** (movement against the gradient using energy in the form of **ATP**). The **Na+/K+ pump** is a classic example of active transport.
 
• **Amphipathic Nature**: Phospholipids are **amphipathic** molecules, meaning they contain both a **polar** (charged) region and a **non-polar** (uncharged) region, which naturally leads to the formation of the **bilayer** in aqueous environments.
 
• **Thickness**: The plasma membrane is extremely thin, with a typical thickness ranging between **5 to 10 nanometers (nm)**, making it visible only under an **electron microscope**.
 
• **Location**: In **animal cells**, it is the outermost layer. However, in **plant cells**, **fungi**, and **bacteria**, it is located just inside the **cell wall**.

questions.question: Carbon can form long chains because it exhibits ________ and shows ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**tetravalency; catenation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Carbon has the unique ability to form bonds with other atoms of carbon, giving rise to large molecules. This property is called **catenation**. These compounds may have **long chains** of carbon, **branched chains** of carbon, or even carbon atoms arranged in **rings**.
 
• The **carbon-carbon bond** is very **strong** and **stable**. This gives us a huge number of compounds with many carbon atoms linked to each other. This is primarily because the **size of the carbon atom** is very **small**, which enables the nucleus to hold on to the shared pairs of electrons strongly.
 
• Since carbon has a **valency of four**, it is capable of bonding with **four other atoms** of carbon or atoms of some other mono-valent element. This property is known as **tetravalency**.
 
• Carbon forms strong **covalent bonds** with **Oxygen**, **Hydrogen**, **Nitrogen**, and **Sulfur**, leading to compounds with specific properties that depend on the elements other than carbon present in the molecule.
 
• In the given question, the first blank refers to the number of bonds carbon can form, and the second refers to the property of self-linking. Therefore, carbon exhibits **tetravalency** and shows **catenation**. ***Hence, the statement regarding option B is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Allotropes of Carbon:**

 
 
• **Diamond**: In this, each carbon atom is bonded to **four other carbon atoms**, forming a rigid **three-dimensional structure**. It is the **hardest known natural substance** and has a very **high melting point**.
 
• **Graphite**: Each carbon atom is bonded to **three other carbon atoms** in the same plane giving a **hexagonal array**. It is a **good conductor of electricity** due to the presence of **free electrons**.
 
• **Fullerenes**: These form another class of carbon allotropes. The first one to be identified was **C-60**, which has carbon atoms arranged in the shape of a **football**. It was named **Buckminsterfullerene** after the American architect **Buckminster Fuller**.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Characteristics:**
 
 
• The **atomic number** of Carbon is **6**.
 
• The **electronic configuration** is **2, 4**, meaning it has **4 valence electrons** in its **L-shell**.
 
• Carbon belongs to **Group 14** and **Period 2** of the **Modern Periodic Table**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Silicon:**
 
 
• **Silicon** also belongs to **Group 14** and exhibits **catenation**. However, it forms compounds with hydrogen which have chains of up to **7 or 8 atoms** only. These compounds are **highly reactive** because the **Si-Si bond** is weaker than the **C-C bond**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Organic Chemistry:** The two characteristic features seen in carbon—**tetravalency** and **catenation**—put together give rise to a large number of compounds. Many have the same non-carbon atom or group of atoms attached to different carbon chains. These were initially called **organic compounds**.
 
• **Historical Context:** It was once thought that these organic compounds could only be formed within a living system through a **vital force** (proposed by **Berzelius**). However, this was disproved in **1828** when **Friedrich Wöhler** prepared **Urea** from **Ammonium cyanate**.
 
• **Isomerism:** Carbon compounds often show **structural isomerism**, where compounds have the same **molecular formula** but different **structural arrangements**. For example, **Butane** (**C4H10**) can exist as a straight chain (**n-butane**) or a branched chain (**isobutane**).
 
• **Saturated and Unsaturated Carbon:**
 
 
• **Saturated compounds** (Alkanes) contain only **single bonds** between carbon atoms and are generally **not very reactive**.
 
• **Unsaturated compounds** (Alkenes and Alkynes) contain **double** or **triple bonds** and are **more reactive** than saturated carbon compounds.

questions.question:
Which of the following is true for solids?

a. Definite shape

b. Rigidity fixed

c. Volume
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a, b and c**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Solids** are characterized by a **definite shape** because the constituent particles (atoms, molecules, or ions) are packed closely together in a fixed, organized manner. The **intermolecular forces of attraction** are very strong, which prevents the particles from moving freely. *Hence, statement a is correct.*
 
• The property of **rigidity** is highly pronounced in solids. Due to the lack of space between particles and strong bonding, they maintain their structural integrity and resist deformation when external force is applied. This makes their **fixed rigidity** a defining physical characteristic. *Hence, statement b is correct.*
 
• **Solids** possess a **definite volume**, meaning they occupy a fixed amount of space regardless of the container they are placed in. Unlike gases, which expand to fill any volume, or liquids, which take the shape of the container while keeping a fixed volume, solids remain unchanged in both shape and volume under standard conditions. *Hence, statement c is correct.*
 
• The **kinetic energy** of the particles in a solid is the lowest among the three primary states of matter. Particles only vibrate or oscillate about their **mean positions**, contributing to the overall stability and lack of fluidity of the substance.
 
• Because all three statements (definite shape, fixed rigidity, and definite volume) accurately describe the fundamental nature of the solid state of matter, the comprehensive answer includes all of them. ***Hence, the correct answer is a, b and c.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **States of Matter:** Matter exists primarily in three states: **Solids, Liquids, and Gases**. While solids have a **fixed shape and volume**, liquids have a **definite volume** but no fixed shape, and gases have **neither a fixed shape nor a fixed volume**.
 
• **Classification of Solids:** Based on the arrangement of particles, solids are divided into two types:
 
 
• **Crystalline Solids:** These have a long-range, regular, and repeating **geometric pattern**. Examples include **Diamond, Quartz, and Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**. They have **sharp melting points**.
 
• **Amorphous Solids:** These lack a regular internal structure and have a short-range order. Examples include **Glass, Rubber, and Plastics**. They are often called **pseudo-solids** or supercooled liquids because they soften over a range of **temperatures**.
 
 
 
• **Incompressibility:** Due to the negligible **intermolecular spaces**, solids are almost **incompressible**. This feature is vital in **engineering and construction**, where materials like **steel and concrete** are used for their ability to withstand heavy loads without changing volume.
 
• **Density and Diffusion:** Solids generally have **high density** compared to liquids and gases because more mass is concentrated in a unit volume. The rate of **diffusion** (the intermixing of particles) is extremely low in solids compared to the other states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Phase Change:** A solid can change into a liquid through **melting** (fusion) and directly into a gas through **sublimation**. The temperature at which a solid turns into a liquid at **atmospheric pressure** is known as its **melting point**.
 
• **Intermolecular Forces:** The strength of the **chemical bonds** (ionic, covalent, or metallic) or **van der Waals forces** determines the hardness and thermal stability of the solid. For instance, the **covalent bonds** in a diamond make it the hardest known natural substance.
 
• **Thermal Expansion:** Although solids have a **fixed shape**, they do expand slightly when **heated**. This **linear expansion** is a critical factor in the design of **railway tracks and bridges**, where gaps are left to accommodate changes in **length** during summer months.
 
• **Modern Physics:** Beyond the three common states, scientists recognize **Plasma** (found in stars) and **Bose-Einstein Condensate** (achieved at temperatures near **absolute zero**) as additional states of matter with unique properties.

questions.question: In a balanced chemical equation, the total number of atoms of each element is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Equal on both sides**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A balanced chemical equation is based on the **Law of Conservation of Mass**, which states that **mass** can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction. Therefore, the total **mass** of the **elements** present in the **products** must be **equal** to the total **mass** of the **elements** present in the **reactants**. ***Hence, statement D is correct.***
 
• In other words, the **number of atoms** of each **element** remains the **same**, before and after a **chemical reaction**. This necessitates that the **number of atoms** on the **reactant side** (left side) is **exactly equal** to the **number of atoms** on the **product side** (right side). ***Hence, statements A and B are incorrect.***
 
• The process of making the **number of atoms** of various **elements** **equal** on **both sides** of an **equation** is known as **balancing** the **chemical equation**. If the **number of atoms** were **always changing**, the **equation** would violate the **fundamental laws of physics**. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect.***
 
• To **balance** an **equation**, we use **coefficients** (whole numbers placed in front of **chemical formulas**). We do not **change** the **subscripts** in the **chemical formulas** of the **reactants** or **products**, as **changing** a **subscript** changes the **identity** of the **substance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Law of Conservation of Mass:**

 
 
• Proposed by **Antoine Lavoisier** in **1789**, this **law** is the **foundation** for all **chemical calculations**. It implies that in any **closed system**, the **total mass** remains **constant** over **time**.
 
• In the **context** of **chemistry**, it means the **atoms** are merely **rearranged** during a **reaction**, not **lost** or **gained**.
 
 
 
• **Skeletal Chemical Equations:**
 
 
• An **unbalanced chemical equation** is often called a **skeletal equation**. For **example**, **Mg + O2 → MgO** is a **skeletal equation** because there are **two oxygen atoms** on the **reactant side** but only **one** on the **product side**.
 
• The **balanced** version would be **2Mg + O2 → 2MgO**, ensuring **two atoms** of **magnesium** and **two atoms** of **oxygen** on **both sides**.
 
 
 
• **Stoichiometry:**
 
 
• This **branch of chemistry** involves using **balanced equations** to calculate the **quantities** of **reactants** and **products**. The **coefficients** in a **balanced equation** represent the **molar ratio** of the **substances** involved.
 
• It is **essential** in **industrial applications** to determine the **exact amount** of **raw materials** needed to produce a **specific amount** of **product**, minimizing **waste**.
 
 
 
• **State Symbols in Equations:**
 
 
• To make a **chemical equation** more **informative**, the **physical states** of the **reactants** and **products** are mentioned along with their **chemical formulas**.
 
• Common **notations** include **(g)** for **gas**, **(l)** for **liquid**, **(s)** for **solid**, and **(aq)** for **aqueous solution** (a **substance** dissolved in **water**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Steps for Balancing:**

 
 
• The **Hit and Trial method** is the most **common technique** used for **balancing simple equations**. One should **start balancing** with the **compound** that contains the **maximum number of atoms**.
 
• Always check the **final equation** to **verify** that the **number of atoms** of each **element** is **equal** on **both sides**.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• A **balanced equation** provides **quantitative information** about the **chemical change**. It tells us about the **number of molecules** or **moles** taking part in the **reaction**.
 
• It is a **fundamental requirement** for solving **numerical problems** related to **chemical reactions** in **science exams** and **research**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of action-reaction pair?

options.text: Swimmer pushes water backward and water pushes swimmer forward
Force of engine on car and car moves forward
Bat exerts force on ball and ball exerts force on bat
Gun recoils backward and bullet moves forward

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Force of engine on car and car moves forward**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton’s Third Law of Motion** states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. This implies that forces always occur in pairs, and a single isolated force cannot exist in **nature**.
 
• In **Statement A**, a **swimmer** pushes the **water** backward (action), and the **water** simultaneously pushes the **swimmer** forward (reaction). These forces act on two different bodies (swimmer and water) and are equal in **magnitude**. *Hence, statement A is a correct example of an action-reaction pair.*
 
• In **Statement B**, the **force of the engine** is considered an **internal force** within the car's system. While the engine generates the power to turn the wheels, the actual movement of the **car** forward is due to the **frictional force** exerted by the **road** (external force) on the tires in response to the tires pushing the road backward. The "force of engine on car" describes a functional process rather than a direct **Newtonian action-reaction pair** between two distinct objects that results in the car's acceleration. *Hence, statement B is NOT an example of an action-reaction pair.*
 
• In **Statement C**, when a **bat** hits a **ball**, the **bat** exerts a force on the **ball** (action), and the **ball** exerts an equal and opposite force back on the **bat** (reaction). This reaction is what causes the **bat** to slow down or vibrate upon impact. *Hence, statement C is a correct example of an action-reaction pair.*
 
• In **Statement D**, when a **bullet** is fired from a **gun**, the **gun** exerts a forward force on the **bullet** (action), and the **bullet** exerts an equal and opposite backward force on the **gun** (reaction). This backward movement is known as the **recoil** of the gun. *Hence, statement D is a correct example of an action-reaction pair.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Force of engine on car and car moves forward.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's Laws of Motion:** These were first formulated by **Sir Isaac Newton** and published in his work **Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica** in the year **1687**. These laws describe the relationship between a body and the forces acting upon it.
 
• **Conservation of Momentum:** The **recoil of a gun** (Statement D) is a classic application of the **Law of Conservation of Linear Momentum**. Before firing, the total momentum is **zero**; after firing, the positive momentum of the **bullet** is cancelled by the negative momentum of the **gun**, keeping the total momentum zero.
 
• **Friction as the Moving Force:** For vehicles like a **car**, the **static friction** between the **tires** and the **road** is the external force that allows for **acceleration**. If the **coefficient of friction** is **zero** (as on perfect ice), the car will not move forward regardless of the **engine's force**.
 
• **Propulsion in Fluids:** The principle of the **swimmer** (Statement A) is the same used by **rowboats** and **jet engines**. In a jet engine, the **exhaust gases** are pushed out of the back at high **velocity** (action), and the gases push the **aircraft** forward (reaction).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Different Bodies:** It is a fundamental **feature** of action-reaction pairs that the two forces always act on **different bodies**. This is why they do not cancel each other out to produce a **net zero force** on a single object.
 
• **Simultaneity:** There is no **time lag** between action and reaction. They occur at the **exact same moment**.
 
• **Nature of Force:** Action and reaction forces are always of the **same type**. If the action is a **gravitational force**, the reaction is also a **gravitational force**; if the action is a **contact force**, the reaction is also a **contact force**.
 
• **Mass Independence:** While the **forces** are equal in **magnitude**, the resulting **accelerations** are usually different because the objects have different **masses** (as per **Newton’s Second Law**, **F = ma**). For example, the **bullet** accelerates much more than the **gun** because the **bullet's mass** is much smaller.

questions.question: What is the process known for removing impurities from ores?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Concentration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Concentration** of ore, also known as **ore dressing** or **beneficiation**, is the mechanical and physical process used to remove **gangue** (unwanted earthy impurities like **sand**, **clay**, and **rocks**) from the mined ore. It increases the percentage of the **metal** in the ore. ***Hence, the correct answer is Concentration.***
 
• **Refining** refers to the final purification of the **crude metal** obtained after extraction processes like reduction. It is not the primary step for removing impurities from the raw ore but from the extracted metal itself. ***Hence, Statement A is incorrect.***
 
• **Roasting** is a chemical metallurgical process where **sulfide ores** are heated strongly in the **presence of excess air** to convert them into **metal oxides**. While it removes some volatile impurities, its primary function is chemical transformation. ***Hence, Statement B is incorrect.***
 
• **Smelting** is the process of extracting a metal from its ore by heating it beyond its **melting point**, usually in the presence of **flux** and a **reducing agent** like **carbon** or **coke**. It involves **chemical reduction** rather than just the physical removal of impurities. ***Hence, Statement D is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hydraulic Washing (Gravity Separation)**:

 
 
• This method utilizes the difference in **specific gravities** between the ore and the gangue particles.
 
• A stream of **running water** is used to wash the powdered ore; the **lighter gangue** particles are washed away, while the **heavier ore** particles settle down. This is commonly used for **oxide ores** of **Iron** and **Tin**.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Separation**:
 
 
• This technique is applied when either the **ore** or the **impurities** possess **magnetic properties**.
 
• The crushed ore is passed over a **conveyor belt** moving over a **magnetic roller**. Magnetic materials like **Magnetite (Fe3O4)** or **Pyrolusite (MnO2)** are separated from non-magnetic gangue.
 
 
 
• **Froth Flotation Process**:
 
 
• This is a widely used method for concentrating **sulfide ores** such as **Galena (PbS)** and **Copper Pyrites (CuFeS2)**.
 
• It is based on the principle of **preferential wettability**, where ore particles are wetted by **oil** (like **pine oil**) and gangue particles are wetted by **water**. **Collectors** and **froth stabilizers** are added to facilitate the formation of a stable froth that carries the ore to the surface.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Method (Leaching)**:
 
 
• This is used when the ore is soluble in a **specific solvent** while the impurities are not.
 
• In the **Bayer’s process** for **Aluminium**, **Bauxite** is treated with concentrated **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)** at **473-523 K**, leaving behind impurities like **Ferric oxide** and **Silica**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gangue**: The unwanted earthly materials associated with ores are called **gangue** or **matrix**.
 
• **Flux**: A substance added during smelting to remove non-fusible impurities by converting them into a fusible **slag**. For example, **CaO** is used as a basic flux to remove acidic **SiO2**.
 
• **Calcination**: Often compared to roasting, **calcination** involves heating the ore in the **absence** or **limited supply of air**, typically used for **carbonates** (like **Zinc Carbonate**) and **hydrated oxides**.
 
• **Electrolytic Refining**: This is a **Refining** technique used for metals like **Copper** and **Zinc**, where **99.9%** purity is achieved by using the impure metal as the **anode** and pure metal as the **cathode** in an **electrolyte**.

questions.question: In flowering plants, the fusion of the male and female gametes within the ovule is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**fertilisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fertilisation** is defined as the biological process of the fusion of **male gametes** (pollen) with **female gametes** (ovum/egg) to form a **diploid zygote**.
 
• In **Angiosperms** (flowering plants), this process occurs inside the **ovule**, which is located within the **ovary** of the **carpel** (the female reproductive organ).
 
• The process begins when a **pollen grain** germinates on the **stigma** and grows a **pollen tube** down the **style** to reach the **micropyle** of the **ovule**.
 
• Flowering plants undergo a unique process known as **Double Fertilisation**, which was first discovered by **S.G. Nawaschin** in the **year 1898**.
 
• In **Double Fertilisation**, one male gamete fuses with the **egg cell** to form the **zygote** (Syngamy), while the second male gamete fuses with **two polar nuclei** to form the **triploid (3n) Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN)**. *Hence, the statement regarding fusion within the ovule describes fertilisation, and option C is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pollination**:

 
 
• It is the **physical transfer** of pollen grains from the **anther** of a stamen to the **stigma** of a pistil.
 
• It is a **pre-fertilisation** event. It can be **Self-pollination** (within the same flower or plant) or **Cross-pollination** (between different plants).
 
• Common agents of pollination include **wind (Anemophily)**, **water (Hydrophily)**, and **insects (Entomophily)**.
 
 
 
• **Transpiration**:
 
 
• This is the **evaporative loss of water** from the aerial parts of the plant, primarily through the **stomata** on the **leaves**.
 
• It creates a **transpiration pull** which helps in the **ascent of sap** (upward movement of water and minerals) from **roots** to **leaves**.
 
• Factors affecting the rate include **temperature**, **light intensity**, **humidity**, and **wind speed**.
 
 
 
• **Germination**:
 
 
• This is the process by which an **organism grows from a seed** or similar structure.
 
• The **dormant embryo** becomes metabolically active and breaks through the **seed coat** to form a **seedling**.
 
• Essential conditions for this process include **water (imbibition)**, **oxygen** for respiration, and an **optimum temperature** (usually between **25°C to 30°C** for most plants).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Post-Fertilisation Changes**:

 
 
• After **fertilisation** occurs, the **zygote** develops into the **embryo**.
 
• The **ovule** matures and hardens its integuments to become the **seed**.
 
• The **ovary** grows rapidly and ripens to become the **fruit**, while the ovary wall becomes the **pericarp**.
 
• Other parts of the flower, such as **sepals, petals, and stamens**, usually wither and fall off.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Endosperm**:
 
 
• The **Endosperm** formed during **Triple Fusion** serves as a highly **nutritious tissue** that provides food to the developing **embryo** during its early stages.

questions.question: Ohm’s Law is valid under which condition?

options.text: For all materials at any temperature
Only for insulator at high temperatures
Only for metallic conductors at constant temperature

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only for metallic conductors at constant temperature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ohm’s Law** states that the **electric current** flowing through a **conductor** is directly proportional to the **potential difference** (voltage) applied across its ends, provided physical conditions like **temperature** and **pressure** remain constant.
 
• The mathematical expression for this law is **V = IR**, where **V** is the **Voltage**, **I** is the **Current**, and **R** is the **Resistance**.
 
• The law is primarily applicable to **metallic conductors** (such as **copper**, **silver**, and **aluminum**) because they exhibit a linear relationship between voltage and current. ***Hence, statement D is correct.***
 
• It is not valid for all materials at any temperature because as the **temperature** changes, the **resistance** of the material also changes, breaking the proportionality. ***Hence, statement A is incorrect.***
 
• **Semiconductors** (like **Silicon** and **Germanium**) do not follow Ohm’s law as they are **non-ohmic** devices where the **V-I characteristic** is non-linear. ***Hence, statement B is incorrect.***
 
• **Insulators** do not conduct electricity under normal conditions and do not follow this linear proportionality, even at high temperatures where their properties might break down. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Origin of the Law:** The law was named after the **German physicist Georg Simon Ohm**, who published his findings in his **1827** treatise, "The Galvanic Circuit Investigated Mathematically."
 
• **Resistance (R):** It is the property of a material to oppose the flow of current. The **SI unit** of resistance is the **Ohm**, denoted by the Greek symbol **Ω**. One ohm is defined as the resistance of a conductor such that a **potential difference** of **1 Volt** causes a **current** of **1 Ampere** to flow.
 
• **Ohmic vs. Non-Ohmic Conductors:**
 
 
• **Ohmic Conductors:** Materials that obey Ohm's law, showing a straight-line **V-I graph** passing through the origin (e.g., **metals** at low/constant temperatures).
 
• **Non-Ohmic Conductors:** Materials that do not obey the law. Examples include **p-n junction diodes**, **transistors**, **vacuum tubes**, **thermistor**, and **electrolytes**. In these cases, the resistance is not constant and varies with the applied voltage or current.
 
 
 
• **Applications:** Ohm's law is fundamental in designing **electrical circuits**, determining the required **resistors** for **electronic devices**, and calculating **power consumption** (P = VI or P = I²R).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Temperature Sensitivity:** For **metallic conductors**, resistance increases with an **increase in temperature** because the **thermal agitation** of atoms increases, leading to more frequent collisions with **drift electrons**. The relation is given by **R = R₀[1 + α(T - T₀)]**, where **α** is the **temperature coefficient of resistance**.
 
• **Limitations:** Ohm’s law is not a fundamental law of nature like **Newton's laws**; rather, it is an empirical description of the behavior of certain materials. It fails under **high electric fields**, very **low temperatures** (superconductivity), or for **unilateral networks** (where current flows in only one direction, like **diodes**).
 
• **Drift Velocity:** The current in a conductor is related to the **drift velocity** of electrons. Under constant physical conditions, the drift velocity is proportional to the **electric field**, which underpins the validity of Ohm's Law.
